ingredients.name: Jalapeño Peppers
ingredients.notes: stemmed, half minced, half sliced for garnish

ingredients.name: Corn Tortillas
ingredients.notes: 6-inch, cut into thin strips for frying

steps.title: Sear chicken and soften aromatics
steps.instruction: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high. Brown chicken in batches until golden but not cooked through, 4–5 minutes per batch; transfer to a plate. Lower heat to medium, cook onion and minced jalapeño with salt until soft, 6–8 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and ancho chile powder; stir 45 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.instruction: Add tomatoes with juice and chicken stock. Return chicken and any juices. Simmer until chicken registers 165°F and shreds easily, 18–22 minutes. Soup should be brothy and deep red-orange — thin with stock if it reduces too far.

steps.title: Shred chicken and adjust seasoning
steps.instruction: Transfer chicken to a board, shred with forks, and return to the pot. Taste and adjust salt — the broth should be savory, cumin-forward, and lightly smoky from the tomatoes, not watery.

steps.title: Fry tortilla strips
steps.instruction: Heat vegetable oil to 350°F in a skillet. Fry corn tortilla strips in batches until crisp and lightly golden, 1–2 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels and season lightly with salt. Hold strips uncovered at room temp up to 2 hours so they stay crisp.

steps.title: Ladle soup and finish at the line
steps.instruction: Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish at the line with tortilla strips, avocado, cilantro, cheese, and lime wedges — garnishes stay separate so late crews get crisp strips. Hold soup at 165°F on the back burner up to 60 minutes; refresh strips if they soften.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Chicken Tortilla Soup for the Hall on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Brothy lime-kissed soup with crisp tortilla strips at the line. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
